we found 348 variables, 342 are new discoveries, 2 are planets, and we provide a catalog of all of them.

we have discovered 348 variable stars in a field towards the Carina spiral arm; we have detected 9 transits in the V -band light curves; and we have discovered 339 new variable stars, among which are eclipsing and ellipsoidal binaries and pulsating stars, as well as stars with flares and other irregular variables.
we discovered a total of 348 variable stars in a deep VLT/VIMOs field in Carina and that 9 of them are transits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the variable star content in the field of the Carina nebula.
a detailed study of the variability in a small but very dense field of the Carina region, which is a part of the Milky Way Galaxy.
the study of the variability properties of stars in the Milky Way and their implications on stellar evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a significant fraction of all variable stars in the Milky Way are still waiting to be discovered, and that a deep and wide survey is needed to find them.
we have detected all variable stars in the magnitude interval between $V \simeq 15$ and $V \simesq 24$ in the field of view of VIMOS.
the VIMOS field in the Carina spiral arm is a good place to find new variable stars, but not new planets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 1 deg ^{2} field can be searched for variables with a depth of $V \approx 24$  mag in about 4 nights with VIMOS on VLT.
the number of known variable stars in the Milky Way has been doubled in a decade, and the number of known pulsators has been tripled in the last 20 years.
we have discovered a significant fraction of variable stars among faint stars, which are not covered by the OGLE project.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VIMOS field in the Carina region contains a significant fraction of variable stars that have not been discovered by any previous survey.
